name: Spina Bifida and Other Spinal Dysraphisms

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Spinal Dysraphism

criteria.description: Identification of spinal neural tube defect on prenatal or postnatal imaging (ultrasound, MRI)
Presence of cutaneous markers overlying the spine such as a sacral dimple, tuft of hair, or hemangioma
Clinical evidence of lower limb motor or sensory deficits consistent with spinal cord involvement
Signs of neurogenic bladder or bowel dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of spinal neural tube defect on imaging plus at least one neurological deficit or cutaneous marker
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Prenatal diagnosis via maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein and detailed fetal ultrasound is common; MRI confirms extent and type.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visible spinal meningocele or myelomeningocele sac
pathognomonic.notes: Most common in open spina bifida

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lower limb motor paralysis or paresis

searchTerms: bladder control issues from nerve damage

common.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata overlying the spine (e.g., sacral dimple, hairy patch)
searchTerms: skin marks over spine like dimples
hairy patches or dimples on lower back

common.symptomName: Orthopedic deformities such as clubfoot or hip dislocation

common.notes: Often associated with Chiari II malformation

searchTerms: sensory loss in feet and legs

occasional.notes: Common in patients with multiple surgeries

occasional.symptomName: Bowel dysfunction including constipation or incontinence
searchTerms: constipation or loss of bowel control

rare.symptomName: Tethered cord syndrome symptoms (progressive neurological deterioration)
searchTerms: worsening nerve problems from tethered cord
progressive neurological symptoms due to spinal cord tethering
symptoms from Chiari II brain malformation

laboratory: Elevated maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein during pregnancy
imaging: MRI demonstrating spinal cord malformation and associated anomalies
genetic: No single gene mutation; multifactorial inheritance with environmental factors (folate deficiency)

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive neurological symptoms without visible spinal defect
Abnormal development of lower spine and pelvis

redFlags: Open spinal lesion with cerebrospinal fluid leakage
Rapidly progressive lower limb weakness or paralysis
Signs of increased intracranial pressure (headache, vomiting) indicating hydrocephalus
